steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: ...There you are, Federico.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Your Holiness.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Did you see the new products on the tea table?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: 'Yvangelista XI Ice Cream Cake Tower'. Eleven scoops of ice cream, eleven flavors of cactus, the eleventh cake named after a pope...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I am a trained executor. I cannot say the same for my ability to evaluate desserts.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Just a token of gratitude, for not forgetting an old man on the brink of death as you withdrew.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Of course, I plan to promote it throughout the city, in the hopes that the people may rediscover the taste of life, sooner rather than later.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Considering the flavor, I suspect it may cause even more controversy.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: It is true, however, that the citizens of Laterano are in dire need of a return to orderly life.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Suicides and crime rates have soared in the past three months.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Small-scale disturbances to large-scale exodus... there are more than a thousand cases in the Notarial Hall's records. The rebuilding of the city has only just begun.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: The calamity has revealed too much and changed too much.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: The Law was a cold machine. Our saint was a loathsome abomination. All of us share the same roots as the devils...

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Any one of these truths is enough to destroy an individual's faith.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: This rebuilding will be a tremendous undertaking.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Reconstruction of the damaged plates on which the Third and Fourth Tribunals are located has just begun. Efforts are underway to revitalize the economy.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Laterano has not been so busy in a long time. I hope that the busy times will provide a way for the people to repair the cracks in their hearts.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Speaking of which... what is your outlook on all this, Federico?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Sankta, Laterano, faith, empathy, communication, and our society... the many important decisions that the Holy City has made overs its millennia-long history, and even your canonization...

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: It was all the result of Him—a machine. The spiritual light has always been cold.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Your innate lack of empathy has bestowed upon you an outlook of extreme logic. Perhaps He chose you because you were the one who could understand the logic of His simulation the best.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: I caught fragments of your conversation with Him.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Even after decades of talking to Him, I must admit... you were more suited to the task.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: If I wasn't intimately familiar with the way you talk, I wouldn't have been able to tell who said what.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: If the Law is a machine, a system, then the most effective method of communication is to think on His terms, with His language and His logic.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: But you arrived at the opposite conclusion from Him.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I remember every word of the tenets, and every name with which I have ever come into contact on my assignments.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: As far as Laterano is concerned, there is no great difference in the order required by machines and life.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The existence of life is a miracle, its two sides the opposing aspects of strength and fragility. Out of necessity, for survival and livelihood, we have continuously built and improved order. The Law is simply part of it.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The Law exists to protect...
Federico pauses. The executor known for his mechanical coldness chooses his words carefully, a rare sight to behold—

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: ...the precious fragility of human life.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Precious fragility... such an interesting combination.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Therefore, we rejected Him. It was our joint decision, Your Holiness. Time will tell whether it was the right one.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Go on.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: My, my. Now that's certainly something.

steps.name: Sankta Nun
steps.text: What is that in your hand, Lemuel?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: A spray can.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: This place is deep underground and cold. This big rock is bare and gray. No wonder everyone who comes here leaves with their head hung low, like they got a heavy cold...

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: I've had enough!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: I'm gonna give it a fresh coat of paint, so people who see it will be happy... wanna join me?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Don't look at me like that! I finished third in the Lungmen graffiti competition two years ago!

steps.name: Sankta Nun
steps.text: You didn't forget what that is, did you?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Just think of it as my way of making a wish! Anything you can't figure out, anything you haven't gotten done, spray it on the rock, and maybe it'll come true!

steps.name: Sankta Nun
steps.text: ...Wish?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Didn't the Sankta and Laterano come about because the saint made a wish?

steps.name: Sankta Nun
steps.text: But it's scrap now...

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: A rock is a rock! How do you scrap a rock?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Besides, you're still here. Me, that girl selling ice cream, that gunsmith over there, and all the Sanktas around are witnesses to your wish...

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Who's to say it's necessarily this rock that grants it?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Think about all the things that've happened these past three months. Any of them would have made the headlines for an entire week in the old days! The entire Holy City has been turned upside-down.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: In the end, though, so many people chose to stay in these ruins... our halos still shine. Life goes on, right?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Just make a new wish! It's not that hard.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: I'll show you how!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Apple Pie Logistics is opening up next week, the first civilians logistics company to be officially recognized by the Curia!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: My wish is that it will grow and grow and have lots of business, and that I'll have lots of time to stay with Mamma and Tata and my sister...

steps.name: Idida
steps.text: Can I make a wish for sugar-free ice cream?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Uh...

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Sure!

steps.name: Idida
steps.text: My wish is that Lateran genetics will change, and everybody will support my culinary research, so that their teeth and halos will never get cavities!
With resilient perseverance, the dawn of a new day shines into the deepest reaches of Laterano, illuminating the green graffiti, and the stone that has long grown dim.
The Sanktas look up. Light dances in the drifting dust.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: ...The Seventh Tribunal proposed a blockade and communications blackout over the area, but the proposal is not feasible.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Hard to block it off when the plates have been so badly damaged.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: The Basilica practically hangs over the side of a cliff. How do you stop curious passersby from looking down?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Besides, the First Saint has already revealed the truth to Laterano... all that our people are doing now is to learn to face it.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Notarial Hall records indicate that the last patient in intensive care at Pagus Faber Central Hospital's Halo Surgery division has been discharged to an observation ward.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Which means that all the non-Sanktas who were given halos in this calamity are no longer troubled by an annoying light over their heads. It only took three months.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: The Sankta halos that were broken are also gradually recovering...

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Empathy continues to exist. It feels different now, but it is still a connection that belongs to the Sankta, and the Sankta alone.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: God is dead, is He not?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: He ordered Andoain and I to destroy Him, and He revealed His weakness to us.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: We destroyed Him with our own hands. I have confirmed that His functions have ceased completely.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: But the program that governs the halos persists...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Is the Law still in effect?

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Let's look at this from another angle, Federico.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: You identified the inherent paradox in the Law. A paradox is a combination of two things that cannot coexist.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: If His last command to you was to eliminate the paradox...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Then perhaps, we have not destroyed the Law itself, but only this erroneous conflict... the paradox itself.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The logic stands, but difficult to process. The machine itself, after all, has ceased to operate.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: You're certainly correct. It was a thought that came to me suddenly as I was chewing on cactus yesterday.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: But I still believe that He left something behind for us.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Perhaps the Law of Laterano was never truly complete. He left behind for us a tabula rasa, waiting for us to communicate with Him.

spans.text: Perhaps the Law of Laterano was never truly complete. He left behind for us a
, waiting for us to communicate with Him.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: That is why I have decided to repurpose the underground structure of the Basilica as a public space, which all citizens are welcome to view as they please.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: Where Laterano goes from here, and what new meaning the Law will create, is a matter in which every Sankta will have their say.

steps.name: Yvangelista XI
steps.text: It is as you said, Federico. Time will tell.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Strange. Where did it go?
The extra grenade launcher maintenance kit is in the bottom drawer. I put the collector's edition disc in the sofa compartment.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Take a break from packing and pour me a cup of cactus juice—I just got back from the hospital, and my throat is parched!

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Take a guess. What do you think happened?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: A Sankta priest just officiated five straight funerals. He suddenly came down with a case of aphasia, while his wife suffered heart pain at the same time...

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: But he was located in an Ecclesia Requietum on the outskirts, while his wife was in a gunsmithy downtown!

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Many similar cases have been reported. Several hospitals and churches submitted a joint report to the Curia last week, detailing the abnormal diagnoses of over a thousand Sanktas...

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: The lights above our heads have come on again, but the strength and range of empathy seem to differ from person to person.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Sanktas unfamiliar with one another only faintly sense each other's emotions, even in close proximity. Friends and family, however...

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: What's your point?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Things seem to have gone back to normal in Laterano, but we both know that fundamental changes have started to take place, after a calamity of such scale.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: You shouldn't leave now, Fia.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: I told you about Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Dr. {@nickname} is here in Laterano, and helped us solve a bunch of problems behind the scenes.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: The Doctor says there's been a major incident at Rhodes Island HQ, and the calamity that struck the Holy City is no coincidence... there is something that links them together, and the Doctor set out on a new journey because of it.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Mostima and I are both Rhodes Island operators. It's our job... and it's for the good of Laterano too.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: I need you to approve my field mission application. You've read the reasons.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: You know what I did, don't you, Fia?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: The Pope decided not to prosecute you. It's not my place to say anything.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Besides, you did help people leave the procession at the very end... you did your duty as a gun-knight.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: People always let an old man off the hook easy.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: It wasn't just you... the abomination had the support of pretty much every Sankta, inside and outside the dream.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: On top of the influence of her empathy, you all had reasons to 'make Laterano a better place'—even if it still sounds dumb, and I still want to call you a sentimental old fool—

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: But I do understand the stuff about parting.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Uh...

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Like I said, there are certain things that I need to experience for myself, even if it does make you worry.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: I'll be back soon.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: All I wanted to say, Fia, is that we didn't get a chance to watch Eight-Armed Chainsaw Guy together yet...

spans.text: All I wanted to say, Fia, is that we didn't get a chance to watch

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Paganini was right. We should try to leave as few regrets as we can, before anything happens.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: You're almost retired, aren't you, old man?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Yeah.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Want to go on a vacation together?

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Finally...
Vannini stands before the door of the gunsmithy. After hesitating for a long while, she takes down the sign that says 'Temporarily Closed', and pushes the door open.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: M-Magister...
Oh, enough with the yelling.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: It's just a halo check. What took you so long? Couldn't be worse than my injuries... *cough*

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Dr. Chandler says my, er, language skills are, getting better.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: He asked me, if I would, consent to be, his research subject... for speech... pathology? And halos—I-I'm not sure I got it...

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: I didn't and I don't care to. You Sanktas are so complicated.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: And you can have your guardian gun back.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: I-Is there a, problem? You weren't around, so I had to, figure it out, best as I could...

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Of course there's a problem.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Wha?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: The grip's too delicate! There's no room for power upgrades! Nothing really wrong with the action design or the assembly work.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: And someone left this bunch of papers at the door. Have a look.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: The Curia's mark... could it be...?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: We're not in the dream. Nobody's closing the shop down.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: It's an order from the Curia. They want us to design heavy firearms for their new gun-knights.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Pa...

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Stop. Of course I know why they came to this tiny workshop.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: You shot him, didn't you, Vani?

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Yeah.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Good girl. Settled an old score for me. Now the past is the past, and I don't want to talk about it again.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: You decide whether to take this order.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: M-Me?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Who else, me? I never expected to still be breathing by now. My chest still hurts. *cough* *cough* I can't see the parts clearly, and I can't hold a barrel firm anymore.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: You made your first gun, and ripped the seal that your Lord placed on your mouth. The hard part is over. The path is yours to walk.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Just don't ruin my reputation...

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: You can do that, can't you?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Yes, El has already left... I told you, it's the Curia's decision.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: This calamity is merely a starting point, for both Laterano and the other nations. We need to recover, and strengthen our ties with the other nations.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: ...El's the best Sankta for the job, considering her experience in Lungmen, and her relationship with Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: She left a message—'Mamma, Tata, let's send Lemuel off on her next adventure with a bang!'

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Let's pray it's not her bowels that go off with a bang... she drank all the cystymilk I left for her in the fridge before she left. Maybe she was worried I would be angry.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Anyway, I've got to go to work.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: This terminal. You're looking at Amos's effects again...

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: They said his last moments were with you?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Yes. I heard his last words, and restored his mailbox history accordingly.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Such a fool, wasn't he?

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Let's cut straight to the chase. What judgment are you gonna pass on my new crimes this time, Cardinal Lemuen?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I take it you admit responsibility for the robbery of that caravan in the western outskirts of the Holy City?

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Don't tell me you couldn't tell they were professional soldiers.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: From Gododdin.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: We're not passing any judgment. The outcome was undoubtedly favorable for the Seventh Tribunal.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: They just caught me in a bad mood.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: The Curia will accommodate Sister Nueda and the Bolívarians who came to Laterano with you.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Regardless of your motivation, your attack on Patrizion worked to our advantage. The Curia sees no need to pursue the matter of your unauthorized return to the Holy City any further.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Oh, what? Laterano still wants to put up a front of purity and clemency, even after waking from the dream. You'll make a show of forgiving a sinner who fell into hell?

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Are you really that stupid?

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: That monster paraded through the streets of Laterano as she gave her speech. It's no secret that angels and devils came from the same place anymore.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: This city's revolting facade has been stripped away.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Without the foundation of its holiness, the 'Holy City' is nothing more than a tiny city-state. Do you think its posturing will continue to win the sympathy of Leithanien or Ursus?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: You misunderstand. Laterano will make no show of clemency.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Your exile still stands. You are not permitted to return to the Holy City. However... the Curia is interested in offering you an employment contract.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Employment?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: To do what you just did.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Hmph. As if the Laterans don't do their own dirty work.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Of course not. Gun-knight, cardinal, Pontifica Cohors, Legatus... nobody is immune to sin. But...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Times have changed. Your judgment was not wrong. Next time, it may not be a scouting force that shows up on the outskirts of the Holy City.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: The most radical transgression in one era may be necessary for survival in another. You were decisive, if nothing else.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Why do you think I would accept?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Can I ask you a question?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: You left Laterano after a big fight with Amos, something that he always regretted... what was the reason for the fight?

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Honey, wh-why are you bringing this up again?

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Yes, Patrizion didn't show up to the wedding, or even give us his blessing... but he's still your mentor.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Is he?

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Besides, it won't change anything—

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: No, it won't. He won't die just because you cursed his soul, and he could even take your job from you...

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: But if you don't even have the guts to do this... then you're a coward, Amos.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: I'm leaving.

steps.name: Aurela
steps.text: Just another pointless argument.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: You've seen the documents in the terminal. I was thinking, maybe the words that Amos left unsaid were...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: No matter what kind of person you are, whether your union was blessed or not, none of that would alter his faith in you—

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: The faith that you were each other's salvation.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: No, I wasn't sure if you would accept the Curia's proposal.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: We all have issues that even empathy can't fully communicate, pasts that we can't let go, and uncertain futures... there is much that I have to think about myself.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: If hatred is what helps you cope, then maybe that's the right path for you.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Perhaps this is what Amos wanted to see.

steps.name: Midwife
steps.text: Still hanging in there, Extra?

steps.name: Extra
steps.text: Argh—

steps.name: Extra
steps.text: I know... I know your heartbeat and... your warmth...

steps.name: Extra
steps.text: I know your fear and your joy...

steps.name: Extra
steps.text: I-If I am blessed by the Law, He shall have mercy on your life...

steps.name: Midwife
steps.text: Praying? Now's hardly the time... wait, you're Sarkaz. Where did you learn to do that?

steps.name: Midwife
steps.text: What the—

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: Did it go well?

steps.name: Midwife
steps.text: Yeah.

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: Then what's with that look on your face?

steps.name: Midwife
steps.text: A h-halo...

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Midwife
steps.text: The Sarkaz's child, that Sarkaz newborn, has a halo...

steps.name: Midwife
steps.text: She said her husband was Sarkaz too, right? The baby's not mixed, like Cecelia...

steps.name: Midwife
steps.text: And we're not in the bloody dream, either. This nomadic abbey is a long way from Laterano...

steps.name: Midwife
steps.text: Where's Andoain?

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: He went out as soon as the abbey stopped. Said he was going to forage, and pick a flower to celebrate the birth of a new miracle.

steps.name: Midwife
steps.text: I have a feeling... he had a premonition about what was going to happen.

steps.name: Midwife
steps.text: Do you remember?

steps.name: Midwife
steps.text: We found Andoain by the pit after the calamity came to a close. He was almost completely blind, and he refused to tell us what happened beneath the Basilica.

steps.name: Midwife
steps.text: A joint court of the First, Fifth, Sixth, and Seventh Tribunals put him on trial. Nobody knows how exactly the trial was conducted, only that he was exiled as a result.

steps.name: Midwife
steps.text: He is never to return to Laterano, but he was allowed to live on this nomadic abbey...

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: Don't think too much about it.

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: It was Andoain's decision to disband the Pathfinders. As he said, we don't need to seek anything from Laterano anymore...

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: Some brothers and sisters have chosen to stay behind in Laterano, while others have returned to their homes. A dozen have chosen to follow him here.

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: Whatever his true hopes for this abbey are, there is at least one thing that is certain—we're trying to help more people...

steps.name: Patia
steps.text: Say, shouldn't he be back by now?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: The Sarkaz learned to pray in that shrine. She established a connection with the Law on her own.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: As for us, we only truly spoke with Him for the first time, after the disintegration of our own faith.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: If faith is a response to life, then a new Law has been born, here and now.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: The crisis has not been averted. Indeed, our rejection of the other possibility has made it even more unknown and pressing—

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Fortunately, a new possibility also lies ahead.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Where will you take it, Andoain?

a.text: The wind carries the cries of the newborn. The Sankta stops on the hill, a wildflower in his hand.
His eyes no longer see, but he continues to look up, standing in the same spot unmoving, as though he can see that tiny speck of light.
After a while, Andoain walks toward the nomadic abbey on the other side of the hill. He leaves Laterano, and never turns back.
No one counts his sins. No one laments the scores of the past. No one sees him off. No one knows of his departure.
There is nothing in his heart that needs resolution. He caresses an aged book, and keeps walking, until he is no more than a tiny point in the vast wilderness.
The martyr shall find final rest at the end of a long journey.
Until then, he shall not rest.
